source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — Godišnji izvještaj banke
why_relevant: Erste's Montenegrin annual reporting page; group-standard disclosure quality, useful benchmark for how EU-parent banks translate CBCG requirements into local disclosure.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — Dokumenta (footer document hub, incl. data-processing and terms)
why_relevant: Consolidated document hub where general terms, fee lists, and compliance/privacy statements are posted; compliance statements here are first-party evidence of how a regulatory obligation is being implemented.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore AD Podgorica — investor & financial disclosures
why_relevant: Domestically owned bank that also issues securities (bond prospectus filed with the Capital Market Commission), so it publishes both banking disclosures and issuer-grade documents — a richer disclosure trail than peers.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica — O banci: izvještaji o poslovanju i novosti
why_relevant: Smaller domestic bank publishing business reports, shareholder information, news and a whistleblowing (zviždači) page — smaller banks are where compliance-cost pressure from new rules shows first.

source_name: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica — opšti uslovi poslovanja i javno objelodanjivanje podataka
why_relevant: Newer entrant publishing general terms for card issuance/use and public data disclosures; useful for observing how a recently licensed bank implements current CBCG disclosure and notice requirements from scratch.

source_name: Universal Capital Bank AD Podgorica — corporate site (terms, tariffs, reports)
why_relevant: Licensed Montenegrin bank in the CBCG register; obliged publisher of general terms, fee tariffs and disclosure reports. Needed for full-market coverage of the regulated-publisher cell.

source_name: Zapad banka AD Podgorica — corporate site (terms, tariffs, reports)
why_relevant: Licensed bank in the CBCG register; same statutory publication duties. Small-bank disclosure practice is a useful indicator of compliance capacity strain under new rules.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Foreign (Turkish) parent bank operating under CBCG licence; publication practice differs from EU-parent peers, useful contrast on how third-country groups meet local notice/disclosure obligations.

source_name: CBCG — Banke u Crnoj Gori (official bank website directory)
why_relevant: Authoritative, maintained list of every licensed bank plus its official website (and banks in liquidation). The canonical seed list for enumerating regulated publishers in this cell and for detecting entries/exits.

source_name: CBCG — Bilansi stanja i bilansi uspjeha banaka / financial statements mirror
why_relevant: Regulator-hosted mirror of each bank's audited annual financial statements in a uniform per-year, per-bank path scheme (…/fin_izv/godYYYY/<bank>_YYYY.pdf). Gives complete, comparable coverage even when a bank site is bot-defended or restructured.

source_name: CBCG — Tarife banaka (comparative overview of payment-service provider tariffs)
why_relevant: Regulator-maintained comparative view of bank fee tariffs, compiled from what banks are obliged to publish. The single best cross-bank tracker of fee/T&C changes without crawling eleven sites, and it directly ties to payment-services transparency rules.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (SCMN) — issuer filings incl. bank prospectuses
why_relevant: Banks that are joint-stock issuers file prospectuses and issuer disclosures here (e.g. Prva banka bond prospectus, Dec 2025). Prospectuses contain regulatory-risk and compliance sections that banks do not publish elsewhere, and are legally warranted.

source_name: Montenegroberza (Montenegro Stock Exchange) — listed-issuer disclosures
why_relevant: Trading venue for Montenegrin bank shares and bonds; carries continuous-disclosure announcements from bank issuers, which surface material regulatory events earlier than annual reports.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore — decisions on fee tariffs and banking secondary legislation
why_relevant: Official gazette carrying the tariff decisions and CBCG by-laws that trigger the bank-side notices this cell tracks; provides the authoritative effective date against which each bank's customer notice can be timed.

source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti / Ostalo (secondary legislation affecting bank disclosure duties)
why_relevant: The disclosure and customer-notification obligations that generate the bank-side documents in this cell originate here; needed to map each bank publication back to its legal basis (e.g. Zakon o kreditnim institucijama čl. 237).

source_name: UBCG — member bank list ("O nama")
why_relevant: Authoritative, cheap enumeration of the full population of licensed banks in Montenegro (11 members observed: Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat) — the seed list for per-bank source scouting. Also enumerates the 16 committees, which is a map of which regulatory topics the sector organises around.

source_name: UBCG — Statut, Program rada and Pregled rada (annual work programme / activity report)
why_relevant: The annual work programme and activity review state, in the association's own words, which draft laws and regulatory files it intends to engage on in the coming year and which it responded to in the previous one — an early-warning calendar for regulatory workstreams and consultation deadlines.

source_name: UBCG — "Bankar" magazine (association journal)
why_relevant: Long-running association periodical (issues into the 70s as of 2026) carrying articles by bank and regulator staff on regulatory change, supervision practice and payments; a rich narrative source on how the sector reads incoming rules, and a named-person directory for the industry.

source_name: UBCG — Propisi (curated banking legislation page)
why_relevant: A sector-curated shortlist of the laws the banks themselves consider core (Zakon o CBCG, Zakon o bankama, Zakon o stečaju i likvidaciji banaka, ZSPNFT, Zakon o platnom prometu, Zakon o zaštiti depozita, Zakon o zaštiti potrošača) plus outbound links to CBCG, Government, securities regulator, court registry and the AML authority — a compact pointer set for the A3 regulatory perimeter.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy of Montenegro)
why_relevant: The statutory chamber is an institutional partner of the Government and a standing channel for business comments on draft legislation; it hosts sector Association Boards (odbori udruženja) including one covering banking, other financial organisations and insurance, and runs a business-barrier reporting tool that surfaces regulatory friction.

source_name: PKCG — Zakonodavstvo / legislation and business-barrier section
why_relevant: The chamber's legislation section is the formal place where its consolidated comments (primjedbe i sugestije) on draft laws and its barrier reports are published — a direct read on private-sector positions during public consultations.

source_name: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore / Montenegrin Employers Federation (UPCG/MEF)
why_relevant: Representative umbrella employers' organisation and official social partner (National Tripartite Agreement, 2006; BusinessEurope member). It publishes formal objections to draft laws with fiscal/financial impact — e.g. it called for the Draft Law on Solidarity Contribution to be withdrawn from public discussion and challenged the Law on Internal Trade amendments on constitutional grounds. Useful as an early, blunt signal on tax/levy measures that hit banks and merchants.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC)
why_relevant: MFIC gathers leading foreign investors (established 2009), including the foreign-owned banks that dominate the Montenegrin market; its members' positions on regulatory and supervisory burden are aggregated and published, and its membership page is a pointer to foreign-capital financial institutions.

source_name: MFIC White Book / Bijela knjiga (annual investment-climate recommendations)
why_relevant: The White Book is the flagship annual compilation of member recommendations on legislation and regulatory practice, typically with a financial-services chapter; it is the closest thing to a standing scorecard of unresolved regulatory grievances, with year-on-year status tracking.

source_name: AmCham Montenegro
why_relevant: AmCham Montenegro runs policy committees and a Policy Manager who coordinates working groups producing position papers and policy recommendations; it participates in the 'Partnership for a Better Business Environment' dialogue with ministries — a structured channel through which financial-sector regulatory positions reach government.

source_name: Montenegro Business Alliance (Montenegro Biznis Alijansa, MBA)
why_relevant: MBA explicitly frames its mission as identifying problems in existing legislative regulation and removing business barriers, and claims a large membership of Montenegrin companies; historically a vocal commenter on regulatory drafts. Its own domain was not confirmed in this pass, so the profile page is recorded as the entry point.

source_name: Nacionalni biro osiguravača Crne Gore (NBOCG) — National Bureau of Insurers
why_relevant: Statutory-purpose association of insurers handling compulsory insurance, Green Card and the Guarantee Fund; its site carries a members section, regulations (propisi) and publications. For sector=both it is the insurance-side counterpart to UBCG and a pointer to the full insurer population.
